candidate.answerReason: The extra 2% tax on income above $28000 equals 0.25% of total income. Hence the excess is one eighth of total income, making $28000 seven eighths of the total and giving $32000, matching B.

methods.label: Compare the tax above the base rate
methods.explanation:
Her overall tax rate is greater than \(p\%\), so some income must be in the higher bracket. Separate the tax into \(p\%\) of all her income and the additional tax on income above \(\$28000\).

The additional tax is \(2\%\) of the income above \(\$28000\). It is also \(0.25\%\) of her total income, because her overall rate exceeds \(p\%\) by \(0.25\) percentage point. Since
\[
\frac{0.25}{2}=\frac18,
\]
the income above \(\$28000\) is one eighth of her total income. Therefore the first \(\$28000\) represents the remaining seven eighths, and her annual income is
\[
28000\div\frac78=28000\cdot\frac87=32000.
\]
At this income, the higher bracket contains \(\$4000\). Its extra tax is \(0.02(4000)=80\), which equals \(0.0025(32000)\), as required. Her annual income was \(\boxed{\$32000}\), choice \(\boxed{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Uses comparison of percentage amounts and division by a known fraction of the whole.

candidate.annotationRationale: The central targets are relating percentage amounts and recovering an unknown whole from a known portion. The method compares the surcharge rates to identify the higher-bracket share, then uses the remaining share to find total income. Percentage interpretation, conversion, and fraction division support this arithmetic route.

review.mathematicalCheck: The surcharge satisfies 0.02(I-28000)=0.0025I. Therefore the excess is I/8, so 28000=7I/8 and I=32000, choice B. The check gives an $80 surcharge under both descriptions.
review.levelCheck: The comparison of percentage amounts and recovery of the whole are elementary. The explanation clearly distinguishes percentage points from relative percentage change.
review.methodDistinctness: One complete arithmetic method is sufficient.
review.annotationCheck: The percentage targets fit the argument. In particular, cnm_p198 applies after identifying $28000 as seven eighths, equivalently 87.5%, of total income. Percentage interpretation, conversion, and fraction division are justified supports.
